Subject: Service signal: throughput drift impacting GREY-Prod hosted inference

Hi Ava / GreyMatter SRE team,

Quick update from Redwood: we observed a gradual throughput degradation affecting GREY-Prod starting ~07:45 PDT. Symptoms we saw: elevated p95 (requests taking 2-3x baseline), intermittent throttling responses (429) for a subset of conversational endpoints, and small increase in retry rates. Impact appears concentrated on higher-concurrency prefix traffic patterns (your integration traces match).

What we did so far:
- Activated tiered fallback routing for GREY-Prod to reduce pressure on the primary pool
- Increased batching worker count in the affected pool by 1.8x
- Applied a temporary kv-cache size bump and pinned hot prefixes for your key tenants

We're continuing to monitor. Rishi is investigating root cause and will share diagnostic traces. I attached an initial p95 graph for your reference (greymatter_p95-traces.png).

Apologies for the disruption — we know you rely on consistent inference timing. I will post updates here as we confirm mitigations/closure.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick technical note from the ops triage:

Preliminary hypothesis: a traffic shift triggered a cascade of prefix cache misses leading to increased KV cache evictions on the primary inference pool. That caused higher per-request latency during KV warmups and amplified batching pressure (longer in-flight requests -> higher p95 and some 429s). We do not see systemic token corruption, so truncated responses are unlikely to be result of model output truncation — they show up as early connection resets in the logs.

Actions taken (in addition to Priya's list):
- Increased per-shard kv-cache by ~40% and forced hot-prefix pinning for several known customer prefixes
- Warmup traffic replays to repopulate caches for the next 20 minutes
- Temporarily reduced max concurrency per-worker to limit queue amplification

Expected timeline: we should see p95 converge back toward baseline in the next 20–40 minutes if cache refill proceeds normally. If you continue to see truncation, please forward a sample request id and timestamps (we'll correlate).

Attaching a short diagnostic extract for your team to review (log excerpt + event markers).

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Service signal: throughput drift impacting GREY-Prod hosted inference — Resolved and next steps

Hi Ava — final update: the immediate incident was resolved at 09:58 PDT. p95 has returned to within normal bounds and retry rates have subsided.

Root cause summary (short): an unexpected traffic pattern produced sustained hot-prefix churn that exceeded our hot-prefix eviction thresholds, causing repeated KV cache misses and amplified batching latency. The chain created transient backpressure on the primary pool and a small number of 429s and early connection resets.

What we're doing next:
- Postmortem in progress; we'll share a detailed timeline, root cause analysis, and permanent mitigations by 2028-05-12 (link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=postmortem-greymatter-20280505)
- Short-term: we've tuned eviction thresholds and added a safeguard to pin prefixes above a traffic-based threshold for 30m windows
- Medium-term: infra team is working on adaptive kv-resizing and an explicit warmup path for hot-prefix arrivals to avoid similar warmup amplification

We've posted an incident snapshot on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/GREY-20280505

We realize any degradation is disruptive — we'll be issuing a small goodwill credit against May usage and will include it in the postmortem. Thank you for the quick coordination and for sending the logs; they helped narrow the cause.

If you want a quick call to walk through the postmortem draft, I can set one up this week (cc Marissa for scheduling).

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
